J U D G M E N T / AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

sentences.text:
The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto LAC no. 77/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Rajbir Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 11 under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

entities.text: Rajbir Singh Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 4//15 (416), 5//11(416), 13//17 (416), 18 (416), 23/2(204), 24(416), 34//25(4 00), 36//2/1(208), 3(416), 4(4 16), 5(204), 7(415), 8(416), 9/1 (215), 12/1(008), 13/1(012) and 14/1(010) i.e. total area measuring 58 Bigha and 04 Biswas, having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
LAC no. 77/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajbir Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 6.

sentences.text:
Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :
i) The said land has school, college, etc. very easily available to the land of the petitioners, thus the land of the petitioners has great potential value being developed and a perfect residentail and commercial site.
The said land is approachable by metaled road and is very close to Nangloi township and Mundka Industrial Area.
These industrial areas were fully developed at the time of issuance of notification U/s 4 of LA Act.
The land is just near to the Mundka Metro Rail Project and therefore was a perfect site for purpose of development of industrial activities.

ii) There are many residential colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Mir Vihar, Jain Colony and Rama Vihar, etc which are existing since 1993 near the land of the petitioner and Govt. is also going to regularise the said buildings and provide all the civic amenities Rajbir Singh (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48692797/
2 thereafter.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the price of the acquired land should have been assessed minimum @ Rs 10,000/- per sq. yards.

iii) The land of the petitioners have been covered by the other revenue estate such as Rani Khera, Madan Pur Dabas, Karala and Mazri which are well developed by way of construction of colonies and have great potential value.

Moreover, the petitioners have solid proof regarding the higher market value of land which is not less than Rs.
10,000/- and the same may be produced at the time of evidence before the Court.

It is also alleged that the Government police has not been properly implemented because the indicative price fixed by the LAC no. 77/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Rajbir Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 Government is totally wrong and illegal and the same should be ratify and compensation be paid to the petitioners.
iv) The land of the petitioner is situated in Village Mubarakpur Dabas and is well connected with metaled roads from all sides and at the time of acquisition was having great potential value as residential and commercial.

entities.text: Rajbir Singh Vs. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The land of petitioner is levelled and as such gives handsome crops income 2-3 times in a year to the petitioner and some part of the land is developed as colony and the petitioners also claims for loss of livelihood and also loss of income interalia on the following amongst other grounds.
v) The land of the petitioner is situated near the National Highway No. 10, Rohtak Road, Delhi and has great potential value as a perfect Building/ Commercial site.
Commercial and Residential activities have commenced all around the land of the petitioner and are going on since more than 12 years.
All kinds of civic amenities like electricity, water, road, bus service, telephone, school, college, etc are easily available to the land of the petitioners,
Thus, the land of petitioners has great value being developed and a perfect residential and commercial site.
iv) The Government Policy has not been properly implemented because the indicative price fixed by the Government is totally wrong and illegal.
Further, the LAC has failed to consider to assessing the value of trees and electric tubewell.
LAC no. 77/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajbir Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 11 7.

yards and Rs. 5 lakhs for damages as sustained by compulsory acquisition and cost of boaring and structure be awarded alongwith statutory benefits and interest under LA Act and enhanced compensation be released to the petitioners and the category of land be rectified.
It is further prayed that the reference as to the inadequacy of compensation may kindly be referred to Ld. District Judge for adjudication.
Petitioners also prayed for the recovery of the cost of the petition alongwith any other order deemed fit and proper be also passed in favor of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 i.e. Union of India and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the said petition as framed is not maintainable, as the petitioner has failed to furnish any evidence in respect of the relief claimed in the present petition and as such merits dismissal.

The Ld. LAC correctly assessed the market value of the land in question prevailing at the time of issuance of notification U/s 4 of LA Act duly considering existing locations, surroundings,
availability of civic amenities and other resources if any, available near the land in question.
The petitioner has not brought any specific and cogent evidence on record to claim a higher compensation as such the order passed by Ld. LAC is a reasoned one and the present petition be dismissed.
It is further submitted that the present petition is false, frivolous and must be dismissed.
LAC no. 77/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajbir Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 11 9.

sentences.text: Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

10. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.
The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
LAC no. 77/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Rajbir Singh Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 11 11.

Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2)
Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).

(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2)
 of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
